summary: The last of sixteen Shawnee lookouts: a steel tower from 1938, cut down in 1973, standing without its cab and closed for repairs in 2026.

facts.design: Steel frame tower; the upper 50 ft were removed in 1973 and an observation platform was built at the top
facts.status_note: Standing, but its cab is no longer in place (Forest Fire Lookout Association).

access.note: Temporarily closed for repairs from May 11, 2026, weather permitting; the Forest Service planned about a month of work and no more than 90 days. Check with the Forest Service before going.

visit.trail_note: Small parking lot at the base of the tower, reached by Trigg Tower Road (Forest Service). The Forest Service release says the observation platform offers visitors views of the Shawnee Hills.

facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service, Shawnee National Forest

events.note: First tower on the site: a wooden tower built by CCC enrollees from Camp Simpson. The register says 40 ft; the Forest Service says 60 ft.
Steel tower built by CCC enrollees from Camp Eddyville replaced the wooden tower. The Forest Service dates the work 1938-39.
Airplanes replaced lookout towers as the main way of spotting fires; the register says the other fifteen Shawnee towers were abandoned and torn down.
Upper 50 ft of the steel frame removed for safety; observation platform built at the top.
Registered on the National Historic Lookout Register on August 28, 2017.
Closed the previous October for protective fencing repairs (year inferred: the report is dated 4 January 2021 and says 'this October'); the report expected the work to run into 2021.
Announced May 4, 2026: temporarily closed from May 11 (weather permitting) for repairs planned at about a month, no more than 90 days.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The 1934 wooden tower and the 1938 steel tower both stood on this site; the record's 1938 date is for the steel tower that stands today. The sources still differ on the wooden tower's height (40 ft in the register and the c.1942 description, 60 ft in the Forest Service page).

notes_for_editor: Access depends on the Forest Service page as read on 2026-10-08, which still showed the site temporarily closed for repairs that were to start May 11, 2026. No reopening notice was found, so check the access line before publishing. The 40 ft vs 60 ft height of the 1934 wooden tower is unresolved; the story shows both. The c.1942 description (40 ft) conflicts with the 100 ft steel tower of 1938; the story says so. The cab status rests on the FFLA list's Standing* note alone; no photo of the cab was read. The 2020 closure year is inferred from the report's 4 January 2021 date line. The NHLR page does not mention climbing; the platform visit rests on the Forest Service release saying the platform offers visitors views. No staffing dates, notable fires or rental listings were found in the sources read. No new photos were added; the existing NHLR photo stays in the record.
